title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
gist: Google's Data Agent Kit is now generally available. It is a free, open-source set of MCP tools and 37 Apache-2.0 skills that connect third-party coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Its guardrails come in two layers: advisory skills such as accidental-data-loss-prevention, and enforced IAM deny policies keyed on tool.isReadOnly. Practitioners note gaps in idempotency and commit status, and Microsoft's Agent 365 enforces governance at a gateway instead.

insights.claim: Google's Data Agent Kit is free and open source, and it installs into coding agents Google does not own: Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VS Code-compatible editors. It is also preinstalled in Cloud Shell and Cloud Workstations.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Google is monetizing agent use through Data Cloud consumption rather than the agent itself, aiming to capture data workloads whichever coding agent wins.
insights.quote: It is free, it is open source, and it installs into coding agents Google does not own.
insights.locator: Google recently made Data Agent Kit

insights.claim: Data Agent Kit combines MCP tools connecting agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services with Google-authored skills, such as optimizing BigQuery SQL or designing Bigtable row keys. The GA release added BigQuery Graph, Bigtable and Managed Service for Apache Spark.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the standard integration layer between AI agents and cloud data platforms.
insights.quote: Data Agent Kit is a set of MCP tools connecting an agent to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services

insights.claim: Google's Arun Nair and Jeff Nelson position the kit as filling a gap: agents write good SQL by default but lack context about which tables exist, how they are partitioned, which ones a team trusts, or why a job failed.
insights.speaker: Arun Nair and Jeff Nelson
insights.so_what: The value in data agents is moving from code generation to live metadata and context access.
insights.quote: which tables exist, how they’re partitioned, which ones your team trusts, or why last night’s job failed.
insights.locator: With the GA release, the company

insights.claim: The Data Agent Kit plugin repository has 37 skills under Apache 2.0. Version 1.0.0 was cut on September 29 and 1.1.0 on October 13, so teams can pin versions, and the kit costs nothing beyond the Google Cloud services used.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Being free removes adoption friction, and Google Cloud consumption revenue is the payoff.
insights.quote: The plugin repository carries 37 skills under Apache 2.0

themes.theme: Advisory guardrails vs enforced IAM controls

insights.claim: The accidental-data-loss-prevention skill tells the agent it must obtain explicit user consent before irreversible operations such as DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, an unscoped DELETE, production bucket deletions, gcloud projects delete or KMS key destruction. This guardrail is only advice that the agent is asked to obey.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Prompt-level guardrails are not enforcement; enterprises adopting agents need hard access controls.
insights.quote: That guardrail is advice. The agent is asked to obey it. A second control is not.

insights.claim: Google enforces read-only agent behaviour in IAM rather than per agent. Teams can run the agent as a read-only service account through impersonation, or apply an IAM deny policy that denies mcp.googleapis.com/tools.call for any tool where tool.isReadOnly is false, at the organization, folder or project level.
insights.speaker: Jeff Nelson
insights.so_what: Reusing existing IAM for agent governance lowers the enterprise adoption barrier and favours Google's integrated security model.
insights.quote: an IAM deny policy that blocks any MCP tool where tool.isReadOnly is false.
insights.locator: Asked in a LinkedIn post whether

insights.claim: The IAM approach has three limits. Blocked tools still appear in tools/list, so agents discover the block only when they invoke a tool. The controls cover only Google Cloud MCP servers. And the resource.service and tool.name attributes are available only in gcloud, not in the console.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Gaps in cross-vendor agent governance leave room for third-party agent security and gateway vendors.
insights.quote: The controls cover Google Cloud MCP servers and nothing else.

insights.claim: viaSocket AI engineer Ankit Dongre argues that MCP access is the easy part. The production boundary is permission scope plus repeat-safe execution, and tool results should carry an idempotency key, commit status and rollbackability, which Data Agent Kit results do not carry today.
insights.speaker: Ankit Dongre
insights.so_what: Reliability, not access, is the unsolved problem for agentic data operations, and an opening for tooling vendors.
insights.quote: MCP access is the easy part. The production boundary is permission scope plus repeat-safe execution
insights.locator: Ankit Dongre, an AI engineer at

insights.claim: AI solutions architect Amel Habira notes that short-lived credentials, the read-only attribute and warnings before notebook cell execution, combined with Iceberg branching and time travel, could enable containment at both the access layer and the data layer.
insights.speaker: Amel Habira
insights.so_what: Table formats with versioning, such as Iceberg, become safety infrastructure for agent-driven data changes.
insights.quote: Combine that with branching and time travel on the Iceberg side, and you can imagine containment at both the access layer and the data layer.
insights.locator: Amel Habira, an AI solutions architect

insights.claim: Timon Knapp, founder of Conductral, recommends starting agents on live systems such as Airflow with read access and suggestions, with a human confirming schedule changes or job reruns, and using audit trails to justify granting more rights later.
insights.speaker: Timon Knapp
insights.so_what: Enterprise agent autonomy will ramp slowly, which tempers near-term expectations for fully autonomous data operations.
insights.quote: I would start with read access and suggestions, and let a human confirm anything that changes a schedule or reruns a job.
insights.locator: Operators are sequencing either way carefully.

themes.theme: Google vs Microsoft agent governance models

insights.claim: Microsoft's Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management, in public preview, keeps governance intent in a Microsoft 365 admin surface and enforces it at a gateway. Per-tool blocking needs a preview tier, and the application key is gateway-scoped. Google instead authorizes per tool in IAM and propagates user identity so that row- and column-level security applies.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The hyperscalers are taking diverging architectural bets on agent governance, which could become a cloud differentiator.
insights.quote: Google authorizes per tool in the IAM language customers already use, and propagates the user’s identity so row and column security applies.
insights.locator: Microsoft put that decision somewhere else.
